html:
"Swedes and Goths" is the map's label, for 800 and 900, for the two peoples of what is now Sweden in the Viking Age: the Swedes around Lake Mälaren and the Geats of Götaland to the south.

The Swedes had their cult centre at Old Uppsala and a trading town at Birka, where the missionary Ansgar came around 829. Swedish Vikings faced east. They crossed the Baltic, went down the rivers of Russia along the route to the Greeks, and brought back Arab silver.

The two peoples came together under one king slowly. Olof Skötkonung, around 1000, is the first known to have ruled both, and the realm grew into Sweden. Swedish kings kept the title "King of the Swedes and the Goths" until 1973. See also West Geats and Viking Age Scandinavia.
